saints.name: Sts. Pontian and Hippolytus
saints.title: Pope and Priest, Martyrs
saints.shortBlurb: A pope and a rival priest who were reconciled and died together in the Sardinian mines…
biography: Pontian governed the Roman Church from 230, while Hippolytus, the most learned Roman writer of his age, had broken with Pope Callixtus I over the absolution of grave sins and let his rigorist party set him up as a rival bishop. The schism he led had lasted some eighteen years when the Emperor Maximinus Thrax struck at the Church's leaders in 235.

Both were condemned to the mines of Sardinia, a sentence meant to kill. On 28 September 235 Pontian resigned the see so that a successor could be elected, the first recorded abdication of a pope, and in that exile the two enemies were reconciled. Pontian died of beatings within weeks; Hippolytus likewise perished in the mines.

Pope Fabian brought their bodies back to Rome, laying Pontian in the papal crypt of the Catacomb of Callixtus and Hippolytus on the Via Tiburtina, and the Church keeps them together on 13 August. Hippolytus is remembered besides for the Refutation of All Heresies and the Apostolic Tradition, which preserves the Church's earliest known rite of ordination.
saints.knownFor: Their reconciliation and shared martyrdom in exile.
